CS 290 / AIP 290

Ethics, Safety and Security in Computing and AI

  • Undergraduate
  • 3 credits

Offered: Fall 2026

This cross-listed course examines ethical, safety, and security decisions in computing and AI. Students evaluate technical and policy evidence and practice communicating their conclusions to technical and nontechnical audiences.

Selected Topics

  • Professional responsibility, fairness, privacy, and stakeholder perspectives
  • Societal and catastrophic AI risks, reliability, and explainability
  • Common AI security failure modes, risk assessment, and defensive safeguards
  • AI governance, standards, regulation, and professional communication

Learning Objectives

  • Identify and analyze ethical, safety, and security risks in AI systems.
  • Apply ethical reasoning and assess possible controls for AI incidents.
  • Develop and communicate governance proposals grounded in technical and policy evidence.

Coursework & Projects

Students analyze cases, complete homework and structured lab activities, and work on a collaborative project about an AI ethics, safety, or security challenge.
